channel.description: Latest articles from West Hawaii Today (westhawaiitoday.com)

item.title: Russia is sharing intelligence with Iran, US officials Say
item.description: WASHINGTON — Russia has provided intelligence to Iran during the U.S.-Israeli war, including satellite imagery showing the locations of warships and military personnel, according to U.S. officials.

item.title: Hawaii men’s basketball beats UC Riverside to earn double bye in tournament
item.description: That roar! was the Hawaii basketball team producing a statement-making 93-74 victory Thursday over UC Riverside at Bankoh Arena at Stan Sheriff Center.

item.title: Lawmaker asks court to block Trump from closing Kennedy Center
item.description: WASHINGTON — Rep. Joyce Beatty, D-Ohio, asked a federal court Friday to block President Donald Trump’s plan to close the John F. Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts for two years starting this summer for what Trump has called a “complete rebuilding.”

item.title: US, Ecuador bomb drug trafficker camp near Colombia border, militaries say
item.description: The U.S. and Ecuador carried out a joint operation targeting drug trafficking operations in the South American country, authorities in both countries said on Friday, with the U.S. calling the move “lethal kinetic operations.”

item.title: Jobs evaporated unexpectedly, a troubling sign for the economy
item.description: Hiring fizzled in February, a sign of unexpected weakness in the labor market that sent warning signs flashing through the broader economy.

item.title: Trump Demands Iran’s ‘Unconditional Surrender’ as
item.description: WASHINGTON — President Donald Trump on Friday demanded Iran’s “unconditional surrender,” the latest and broadest expansion of his goals for the war, while Israeli jets pummeled Tehran and other parts of Iran with a fresh wave of airstrikes.

item.title: Democrats blame Trump for weak jobs report as Republicans play defense
item.description: Democrats warned Friday that an unexpectedly poor jobs report signaled that the economy could sink into a recession, casting the downturn as a consequence of President Donald Trump’s decision to focus on foreign entanglements rather than issues at home.

item.title: BIIF baseball and softball: Waiakea, Hilo sweep opponents; KSH and HPA post shutouts
item.description: The Big Island Interscholastic Federation (BIIF) spring sports season continued this week with a full slate of softball and baseball games.

item.title: Former US Rep. Colleen Hanabusa dies at age 74
item.description: Colleen Hanabusa, a former state lawmaker and prominent labor lawyer from Waianae who served in Congress but failed at bids to become Hawaii’s governor and Honolulu’s mayor, died today, her family confirmed. She was 74.
